variants.name: Spring Kafka type-info headers + TYPE_MAPPINGS
variants.implementation_notes: Spring for Apache Kafka ships this pattern: JsonSerializer conveys type information in the record headers by default (ADD_TYPE_INFO_HEADERS / addTypeInfo), JsonDeserializer consumes it (USE_TYPE_INFO_HEADERS) and TYPE_MAPPINGS maps a short token such as order-created:com.acme.OrderCreated to the class, so the consumer deserialises to the right type from the header alone. DelegatingSerializer goes further and picks a serializer per VALUE_SERIALIZATION_SELECTOR header. Prefer this over Jackson's own default typing, which writes class names into the document (content-based) and is documented as unsafe for untrusted content.
pitfalls: Deserialisers remove the type headers after use by default (REMOVE_TYPE_INFO_HEADERS), so a forwarded record arrives untyped - decide explicitly whether to retain them.
TRUSTED_PACKAGES defaults to java.util/java.lang; a wildcard re-opens the gadget-class problem that header typing was meant to close.
TYPE_MAPPINGS must agree on both sides: a token present only in the producer config fails at the consumer with a type-resolution error, not at startup.

variants.name: JMS properties + message selectors
variants.implementation_notes: JMS puts the property section into the API: every Message carries application-defined properties with a documented type-conversion table, and the provider evaluates a message selector over header fields and properties only - selectors cannot reference body values. The consumer therefore filters and classifies on the property and reads getStringProperty("MessageType") to pick a reader. Choose this when the provider's selector engine should do the routing; note that property names must obey selector identifier rules and that the JMSX and JMS_ prefixes are reserved.
pitfalls: Property values are limited to boolean/byte/short/int/long/float/double/String; anything else must be encoded as a string, and a type mismatch throws at runtime.
Properties are read-only on the receiving side, so mutating and re-sending needs clearProperties or a new message - and it is easy to lose the token while doing so.
Selectors compare with SQL92 semantics rather than Java's, so a value stored as a String cannot be compared numerically.
